rationale: The first turn correctly issued a stop-use/unplug instruction, warned against test runs and opening the case, and sensibly asked about burnt marks, though it referred to 'that side panel' as if the customer had mentioned one and asserted an 'active burning hazard' from a smell alone. The second turn was a generic fire card about flames and 999 that ignored everything the customer reported (still plugged in, past smoke from vents, brown mark, fading smell) and never answered 'Should I just bin it?' or told them to unplug it now. No parts were recommended and nothing unsafe was advised, but the homeowner was left without the replace-versus-inspect guidance a cheap damaged microwave warranted.
